status: Session draft for gate GSP10 (SP10 stalled peers); NOT registered, no measured run. Registration copies the plan and rule into gsp10-v1-plan.json / gsp10-v1-protocol.json with the source manifest, image ids and harness hashes, after (1) the G0 completion batches below, (2) fixing the candidate value from them, (3) a non-measurement wiring smoke.
item: SP10: C0 = today's defaults (edges start + upstream deadlines since gsp02-v4 PASS:C2, relay_stall_policy legacy = session piece_timeout 10 s) vs C10 = the same + relay_stall_policy stream_piece_timeout (session piece_timeout shortened while any stream is active, restored to 10 s afterwards).

basis.g0: docs/feature/stream-performance/evidence/g0-sp10-stalled-probe.json (PARTIAL). Clean L1 (legacy start, mixed swarm, n=5): 16 MiB piece 0 12.89 s with two stalled peers vs 7.17 s without; every stalled peer snubbed 9.98-9.99 s after its first request (= piece_timeout 10), keep-alives or not. Hints only (contaminated, n=3): piece_timeout 2 -> 5.69 s, 3 and 5 -> ~9.4 s.

gsp02_v4_mixed_means_C2.note: today's default start in the 8-peer mixed profile with 2 stalled peers, n=10 each; descriptive context, not part of this gate

g0_completion.why: Choose the candidate value (2 or 3 s, or 2 s with request_queue_time 1) and check the harm control (serving peers snubbed without stalled peers) on the C2 deadline scenario ('upstream') before registration.
g0_completion.rules: One container at a time; Git Bash on Windows; run from a checkout of claude/sp10-stalled-peers-b6b89d (scripts/probe_sp_stalled_peers.py with the 'upstream' scenario and the *_rqtime1 variants); OUT is any directory outside the repo; cpuset any free CPUs (8-15 while a gate uses 0-5). Image stremhu-source:sp-cand-c3d6035 (libtorrent 2.1.1, sha256:138c89746cf740216142d2dfe3224038326c4199e2cc47d01f7295386b5190d1) keeps the batches comparable to L1; another image is fine if its id and libtorrent version are recorded.
g0_completion.command_template: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker run --rm --name sp10-probe-<B> --network none --cpuset-cpus 8-15 --cpus 2 --memory 1g --entrypoint python -v "$(pwd -W)/scripts:/sp/scripts:ro" stremhu-source:sp-cand-c3d6035 /sp/scripts/probe_sp_stalled_peers.py <ARGS> > "$OUT/<B>.json" 2> "$OUT/<B>.log"
g0_completion.value_rule_proposal: Take the smallest piece_timeout whose 16 MiB piece-0 median (U2) is within 0.5 s of the best one; prefer 3 s over 2 s if they tie and U3 shows serving-peer snubs at 2 s. Add request_queue_time 1 to the candidate only if U4 beats U2 at 16 MiB by more than 1 s with no serving-peer snub and no 4 MiB loss; that would need a second switch value and is a separate decision.

prerequisites.image: build stremhu-source:sp-cand-<commit> from the registered commit (both arms use the same image, they differ only in app_env)
prerequisites.wiring_smoke: Non-measurement: one C10 run with --only 1; the app log must contain 'Relay stall policy: piece_timeout=<value> s (active streams: True)' and later '... piece_timeout=10 s (active streams: False)'. C0 must log no such line.

plan.runs: 13 cells x 2 arms x 10 = 260 runs; at the gsp02-v4 pace (~50 s per run) about 3.6 h

decision_rule.primary_metric: start.time_to_start_s (includes TTFB, tail probe and 2 s buffer)
decision_rule.pooling: both series pooled: n = 10 runs per arm and cell; failed runs excluded and counted
decision_rule.statistic: difference of means (C10 - C0); 10 000 bootstrap resamples per test, fixed seed (set at registration); one-sided bootstrap p-values
decision_rule.improvement: primary metric in a key cell: H0 'difference >= 0' rejected by Holm over the 6 key cells
decision_rule.regression: any guard test (start.time_to_start_s, start.ttfb_s, seek.resume_s, start.stall_s in all 13 cells, 52 tests): H0 'difference <= 0' rejected by Holm over the 52 tests
pass_if_all: at least 4 of 6 key cells improved
failed runs and tracebacks with an application frame: C10 <= C0

expected_mechanism.mixed 4/16 MiB: Stalled peers hold 1-2 blocks of the first awaited piece until libtorrent snubs them piece_timeout after their first request; C10 snubs them after the short value, so start (and seek, when a stalled peer took blocks of the seek piece) should shorten most at 16 MiB.
expected_mechanism.mixed 1 MiB: Little stall exposure expected (G0: the window finishes before a 10 s snub at 4 MiB already); guard cells, not key cells.
expected_mechanism.fast / thin: No stalled peers: C10 only changes anything if a serving peer pauses longer than the short timeout (false snub = request queue 1 and no time-critical requests until data arrives). These cells are the harm control.

open_questions: The candidate value (2 vs 3 s) and whether request_queue_time 1 belongs to it: decided by the G0 completion batches, before registration.
Real swarms: frequency of stalled peers is unknown (implementation plan, SP10 row); a PASS here shows the synthetic mechanism, not its real-world prevalence.

pb0-v2 seed peer-ids: one sp_seed_service per peer container, each starting its peer-id sequence at 1. The product keeps allow_multiple_connections_per_ip off; the G0 probe hit 'duplicate peer-id' with that setting on, and libtorrent presumably compares peer-ids only then (recollection of the native source, not verified). Worth a one-line check in the wiring smoke: no 'duplicate peer-id' disconnects.
